First-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_013ELWDeai2Y6Wqrh7DmkUV6`): promoted out of `finding` into the decision inbox. `domain:devx` kept — the roster/gate half lands in `scripts/`. This card is made the **parent** for the shared prior question; #10920 (the runtime-surface instance) is being marked `pm:blocked` against it rather than entering the inbox separately, per the same-family meta-criterion.

Why it is not queueable as filed: the body's three shapes each **widen what a gate accepts** (a roster admits fenced examples the current fence forbids; a probe decides admission from the network). That is the mechanical boundary test for the manual floor — accepted-set expansion — so no seat rules on it.

[facets-block] 四棱分析(业务视角)

**一句话问题**:我们公开的文档和产品运行时提示里,可以出现「这个仓库不构建的 `@objectstack/` 包」吗?可以的话,它从哪发布这件事记在哪?

**客户可感知的代价**:今天 `packages/console/README.md` 的第一条安装指令是 `pnpm add @objectstack/framework`,而这个包不在本仓任何目录里。它要么真的在别处发布(那我们只是没记录),要么**我们的头号安装指令是坏的**。读者分不出来,gate 也分不出来。同类还有三个:CLI 会打印 `pnpm add @objectstack/security-enterprise`(且有测试 pin 住这句话)、`serve.ts` 让运维加 `@objectstack/organizations`、spec 常量注释指向 cloud 仓的 `@objectstack/service-tenant`。

| 选项 | 客户端效果 | 我们付的代价 |
|---|---|---|
| **A** 建声明式名册(一行一个仓外包 + 它从哪发布) | gate 能放行真实仓外包的可运行示例,读者能查到出处 | 多一个必须保持真实的文件 |
| **B** 只允许散文提及、机械强制(#10893 后的现状) | 永远不能为一个真实在别处发布的包写可运行示例 | 零成本,但把一条合法用例永久关死 |
| **C** 联网查 registry 判定 | 自动、永远准 | 把这族刻意离线的 gate 拉上网(限流、离线 CI 失效) |

**行业类比**:像文档里写「请安装我们的企业版插件」,但公司内部没有任何一张表说明企业版插件由哪个团队发布、发布到哪 —— 客服和文档作者只能互相打听。

① **实际业务需求**:这四个名字里至少一个(`@objectstack/framework`)是**安装指令**,不是顺带提及,而且被 CLI 的一条测试 pin 住。⚠️ 但这一半严格说不是决策题,是**没人查过的事实题** —— 见下面的推荐。
② **项目长远合理性**:A 把「仓外包」从口头知识变成声明,与 contract-first 同向;B 永久禁止一类合法用例;C 破坏这族 gate 一致的离线设计,为一个问题引入一整类新故障。
③ **防 AI 写错**:今天读者和 gate 都区分不了「仓外包」与「凭空捏造的包」—— AI 会照抄 README 里的 `pnpm add`,这正是批量犯错被掩盖的温床。A 的「声明即强制」最对症;B 至少保住 gate 的响亮拒绝;C 把判断权交给网络。
④ **创业阶段不扩散**:B 零成本;A 一个文件加一份保持真实的义务;C 最贵。

**推荐:先答事实,再选形状。** 四个包到底发布没发布、发布在哪,这个读数一旦有了,选项就塌缩了 —— 如果它们真在别处发布,A 几乎是唯一诚实的选择;如果一个都没有,那这些根本不是治理问题,是**四处文档/运行时错误**,按 B 修文本即可,连 ruling 都不需要。⛔ 不推荐 C。

**本分析看不见什么**:① 本席无法从仓内查 npm registry,四个包的发布状态是零读数,而它决定 A 与 B 谁对;② `cloud` 仓不在本会话的 GitHub 授权面,`@objectstack/service-tenant` 的归属无法自查;③ `@objectstack/framework` 是否是伞包(umbrella)发布名,本仓无任何记录。

**裁决格式(低摩擦)**:你如果**知道**这四个包发布在哪,回一句话就够了 —— 我据此直接路由(有出处 ⇒ A 建名册;没有 ⇒ B 修四处文本)。你如果**也不确定**,回「查」,我路由一张 S 级测量卡(查这四个名字的发布状态与出处)进 `domain:devx` 队列,本卡挂 `Blocked-by:` 等它。也可以直接回 A / B / C 覆盖以上。

裁后执行段:本卡裁定落地时,**同笔解除 #10920** 的 `pm:blocked`(它等的是同一个前置事实,不会自己解锁 —— 本卡即使转成工作态仍是 open,解锁扫描看不见)。

## The ruled measurement is taken — and the fork collapses **mixed**, 3 fabricated / 1 real

The maintainer's ruling of 2026-08-22 (`5377356971`, from the 46-card digest accepted 「接受所有」) made this card's first step a measurement: *"establish the publication status and provenance of the four out-of-repo names"*, with the A/B fork decided by the result and **option C not taken**.

The triage analysis said it could not take that reading — *"本席无法从仓内查 npm registry,四个包的发布状态是零读数,而它决定 A 与 B 谁对"*. This seat can. Taken 2026-08-23T06:2xZ, unauthenticated `GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@objectstack%2F<name>`:

| name | registry | verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@objectstack/framework` | **404** | not publicly resolvable |
| `@objectstack/security-enterprise` | **404** | not publicly resolvable |
| `@objectstack/organizations` | **404** | not publicly resolvable |
| `@objectstack/service-tenant` | **200**, `dist-tags.latest = 4.1.0` | **real, published** |

**Positive control, because a bare 404 proves nothing on its own:** `@objectstack/spec` → **200**. So the endpoint works, the `@objectstack` scope is publicly readable, and `service-tenant` returning a real version from that same scope proves an out-of-repo package *does* publish there. The three 404s are therefore a reading about those names, not about my access.

⚠️ **The one caveat, stated rather than glossed:** npm answers 404 for a *private* package as well as a nonexistent one, and this probe is unauthenticated. So the strict claim is **"not publicly resolvable"**, not "does not exist". For three of these that distinction does not rescue the text, because the operative fact is identical: **a public reader who runs the command we print cannot install it.**

### What this makes of the four cases

**Three are broken instructions we ship to users** — and these are not passing mentions, they are commands:

- `packages/console/README.md:3,13,25` — `pnpm add @objectstack/framework` is the **first install instruction of a published README**.
- `packages/cli` **prints** `pnpm add @objectstack/security-enterprise` as a capability hint, and `packages/cli/test/capability-preflight.test.ts:74` **pins that string** — so the test currently guarantees we keep telling users to install a package they cannot install.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:2423` tells the operator to add `@objectstack/organizations`.

**One is real** — `@objectstack/service-tenant@4.1.0`, exactly as `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts:132-134` describes it (contributed by the cloud runtime, defined in the separate `cloud` repo). Its prose is **correct** and must not be "fixed".

### How that lands against the ruling

The ruling: *"packages that really are published elsewhere collapse the choice toward A (a declared roster with provenance); if none are published, this is four documentation/runtime text errors to be fixed under B's shape."* The measured world is **neither pure branch** — it is one of each — so the honest reading of the ruling is that both of its arms fire, each on its own rows: **B for the three fabricated names** (fix the text, and the test that pins it), and, for `service-tenant`, the provenance question A exists to answer. Because that is a population of **one**, whether it earns a roster *file* is a live judgement rather than a foregone A; a card dispatched off this comment should say which it chose and why, and is free to conclude that one row does not need a registry.

⭐ Worth stating plainly, because it reprices this card: it was filed as a governance question about where a roster lives. The measurement says the sharp half is not governance at all — **three customer-facing install commands name packages the customer cannot install**, one of them defended by a passing test. That is the finding.

⛔ Not acted on here beyond the reading. Dispatch follows from this seat in the same round; `#10920` waits on this same prior fact and is unblocked by whatever lands, per the ruling's standing execution note.

Seat `devx@objectstack`, session `session_01SPBxLsqQGCVL5z5UXvgipH`.

## ⚠️ PM correction — my reading on `5384607091` was wrong on two of the three, and the caveat that catches it is one I wrote myself

The dev re-took the measurement and reached a different split. It is right and I am recording that here rather than only in the PR, because my comment stands on this card as a confident finding another seat could act on.

**My numbers reproduce exactly.** `framework`, `security-enterprise`, `organizations` → 404; `service-tenant` → 200 at `4.1.0`; positive controls `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/cli` → 200. Nothing about the registry reading changed.

**What was wrong is the inference.** I treated three 404s as three fabricated names. I even wrote the caveat that refutes that — *"npm answers 404 for a private package as well as a nonexistent one, and this probe is unauthenticated"* — and then reasoned in the very next paragraph as if it did not apply. It applies to two of the three.

| name | my reading | measured against the tree |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@objectstack/framework` | fabricated | **fabricated** ✅ |
| `@objectstack/security-enterprise` | fabricated | ❌ **real, deliberately private** — declared *with provenance* in `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` as `edition: 'enterprise'` |
| `@objectstack/organizations` | fabricated | ❌ **real, deliberately private** — "closed-source" (`serve.ts:2576`), "cloud-private" (`serve.ts:228,253,2618`, `verify/src/harness.ts:44,153,466,487`), one citing `cloud#1013` |

Verified independently from this seat on `origin/main` before accepting the correction — I did not take it on the dev's word:

- `packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts:121` really does export `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` with `package` / `edition` (`open`\|`cloud`\|`enterprise`) / `note`, and `:60` records that `hierarchy-security` ships in `@objectstack/security-enterprise`.
- `git grep` returns **eight** sites calling `@objectstack/organizations` closed-source or cloud-private across two packages.
- `@objectstack/framework`: **no workspace package of that name exists**, and `packages/console/README.md:25` presents it as the *default public* install — *"Default install for `@objectstack/framework` consumers"*. Nothing anywhere calls it private or enterprise. So that one is genuinely a public install command for a package no reader can install.

**So "three broken install commands" is wrong; it is one.** The other two are real packages whose hints already carry their edition boundary, and "fixing" them would have been precisely the vacuity this card warned about.

## ⭐ And option A is already built — which is a better answer than the one I proposed

I suggested a population of one might not earn a roster *file*. The dev found the roster **already exists**: `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` is exactly *"one row per out-of-repo package with where it ships"* — `package` + `edition` + a prose `note`, drift-tested against the capability vocabulary and read by both the CLI preflight and cloud's runtime. Three out-of-repo packages already have rows.

So the right move was to add **no** roster, no gate and no `check:` alias — a second one would be the failure that file's own header names: *"A second description nobody checks is how that happens; one exported list is how it stops."* That resolves the ruling's A/B fork better than either arm as written: **A's artifact was already there.**

The one genuine gap — `@objectstack/organizations` has no row, because the map is keyed by `requires` token and that package is `plugins[]`-wired off the tenancy posture — needs a `packages/spec/**` edit, which I fenced out of this card. Correctly routed to **#11263** for the spec seat instead of being done here.

This is the second time this round a dev re-derived instead of building on what I handed it, and the second time that is the only reason a wrong reading did not become a wrong change. The dispatch asked to be falsified; it was.

Seat `devx@objectstack`, session `session_01SPBxLsqQGCVL5z5UXvgipH`. ACCEPT for PR #11266 follows once its CI converges — currently green-so-far and still running.
